assumptions: The SPEC-069 driver works for Codex inside the Lightning profile. The SPEC-071 consent gate is host-agnostic. Codex CLI 0.162.0 or newer is the supported stream shape. SPEC-087 registry code exists before this change. The Lightning host-site inventory recorded at 65f101ba is complete.
compatibility: Additive for Codex. Defaults, stored records, digests and outputs for claude-code and opencode are unchanged; a reader that predates the change refuses Codex records. Rollback removes codex from the capability and tables and deletes the fixture.
domain: The Braid Lightning host path in agent_braid/lightning_*.py and the SPEC-087 registry at the recorded commit; one Codex build as observed by T003.
execution_contract: None until T011. The change runs fake hosts only; a real Codex rollout is a separate task that needs the owner's explicit yes. executionAuthorization stays false in every plan output.
observation_contract: The differential record of claude-code and opencode outputs taken from develop before the change (T002) and Codex stream observations recorded by T003; equality of bytes and sets after the change. Equality shows no change for existing hosts at one commit, not that Codex works.

scenarios.then: each open question is decided or deferred in a dated record and the spec is approved, amended or rejected.

scenarios.then: it returns `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex` in that order; and given the SPEC-087 guard test, when it runs, then it passes with no new exception file.

requirements.text: Codex joins `lightning-run` through the registry.. `codex` is added to the `lightning-run` capability of the SPEC-087 registry (its REQ-002, REQ-006), appended after the current members so the order is `claude-code`, `opencode`, `codex`. Each Lightning site that today lists the two hosts reads that capability, and no module outside the registry and SPEC-087's exception files declares a new literal collection of host identifiers (SPEC-087 REQ-010). The capability name may be renamed by SPEC-087 T001; this specification follows the name merged there.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T004, T006, T007.
scenarios.then: each key set equals its capability query; and when `codex` is removed from one table, then the test fails.

requirements.text: Feature-owned tables gain Codex.. The runner's credential, fake-binary and binary tables, the schema, config and export-terms host checks, and the declared-limit table of REQ-008 each cover exactly the `lightning-run` members, and a key-set test pins each to the capability (SPEC-087 REQ-009). `META_TOOLS` and `PARSERS` (`lightning-tool-classes`) keep their three keys. Per-host credential variable names, binary names, parsers and tool prefixes stay in `agent_braid/lightning_*.py`, never in the registry (SPEC-087 REQ-009).

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T004, T005.
scenarios.then: it is refused with `config-enum` and nothing is launched; given `opencode`, then it passes configuration and is refused at launch as today; and given `claude-code`, then it is accepted as before.

requirements.text: Optimizer path unchanged.. The registry gains a capability `lightning-optimizer-config` whose members are today's optimizer enum, `claude-code` and `opencode`, in that order; `optimizer.host` and the CLI `--optimizer-host` accept only its members. `codex` is not a member, so `optimizer.host: codex` ends in the existing configuration refusal (`config-enum`) before any run. `SandboxedHost` stays the only later gate and keeps refusing every host but `claude-code`, so `optimizer.host: opencode` behaves exactly as today. Codex MUST NOT serve optimizer calls (OD-2).

requirements.text: Existing hosts and defaults unchanged.. The default `rollout.hosts` is the registry capability `lightning-default-rollout`, whose members are `claude-code` and `opencode`, in that order; it is no longer derived from the whole `lightning-run` tuple, and Codex is opt-in by naming it. The wizard prompt text of `lightning_cli.py:26` is unchanged. For every configuration, preview, run, plan, record, report and refusal that does not name `codex`, the output bytes, digests and refusal codes are identical to those before the change. The one exemption is refusal and usage text that lists the accepted hosts, which may additionally list `codex`.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T005.

requirements.text: Additive schema acceptance.. `codex` is accepted additively in the `host` fields of the rollout, model-identity and `attempt_start` records. Schema version strings (`v0.1`) do not change, no stored record is rewritten, and a Codex record read by a reader that predates this change is refused (fail closed) (OD-4).

scenarios.given: a Codex rollout (fake host) with a provider key in the environment
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T003, T006, T011.
scenarios.then: it is refused with `paid-route-refused` before launch; given a Codex transcript that reports no credential source, then the verdict is `route-unverified`; and given the source observed by T003, then only that value is accepted and any other value ends as `route-unverified`.

requirements.text: Subscription route, same bar as the other hosts.. A Codex rollout runs only on the subscription route: the existing pre-launch gate refuses any provider key or route variable (`paid-route-refused`, including `CODEX_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`), the runner reads no credential file and writes no credential, and any credential value is held in the environment of the child only and registered with the secret scanner (SPEC-071 REQ-004, REQ-005). After launch the runner accepts a Codex credential source only from a field the host itself reports or from an observation that T003 records and the owner reviews; it does not infer the route from the profile or from the absence of a key (OD-3). Until that evidence exists the key-source verdict for `codex` is `route-unverified`.

scenarios.given: a run of `claude-code` and `codex` where Codex reports no source
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T006.
scenarios.then: `claude-code` has its normal records, `codex` is a declared limit, and the run status carries no refusal; and given a `claude-code` `route-unverified`, then the run still stops as today.

requirements.text: Unverified Codex route is a declared limit.. When Codex ends as `route-unverified`, the run records `hosts.codex.status = declared-limit` with the reason text, does not set a run-level refusal, and continues with the remaining hosts, as it does for `opencode` today. The set of hosts that end this way is a feature-owned table keyed by the `lightning-run` members, not a literal comparison.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T003, T007.

requirements.text: Codex transcripts are parsed from observation, not assumption.. Before any real Codex rollout, `parse_codex`, the Codex tool-name prefix (`agent-braid__`) and the tool-class decision are checked against recorded Codex streams, and the model-identity source of a Codex rollout is recorded; an unknown model is recorded as unobserved, never guessed. The verification is written as obtained evidence and states the Codex build it covers.

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits. Planned for tasks T006, T008.
scenarios.then: the pipeline completes through the fake-only source, every record is labelled `pipeline-only`, no network or provider access occurs; and given the same stream with `fake_hosts` false, then the verdict is `route-unverified`.

requirements.text: Fake Codex host for the pipeline.. `--fake-hosts` can run Codex through a fixture `tests/fixtures/lightning-fake-hosts/codex`, labelled `pipeline-only` like the existing fixtures, so CI exercises the Codex path without a Codex install, a model or quota. Because `parse_codex` reports no credential source, a fake Codex rollout completes only through a key-source value that exists solely in the fake-host path (set by the fixture, accepted only when `fake_hosts` is true, recorded with the `pipeline-only` label) and never in a real run; the production verdict of REQ-007 is not weakened, and a test runs the real verdict on the same stream to show it ends as `route-unverified`.

Only a later amendment, backed by Codex measurements, can make Codex binding.

requirements.text: Codex runs on the development set only.. The runner allows a `codex` host only for the prompt set `development` and refuses it before launch for every other prompt set: the SPEC-069 `held-out` set (spent), the SPEC-078 and SPEC-079 splits (`v2-feedback`, `v2-validation`, `v2-test`, `v3-test`, `v4-test` and their freezes) and any set added later. This is an allow-list, so a new set is refused by default. A fresh preregistered split is SPEC-089's. The refusal reuses an existing code or adds one to the closed vocabulary of SPEC-071's refusal contract in the code phase.

scientific_limits: Engineering, not a research protocol. No claim that Codex meets D4, is valid, or is on a subscription route; parse_codex is verified only for the observed Codex build and event shapes. A passing profile is not human review or approval.
scope: Specify Codex as a Braid Lightning rollout host through the SPEC-087 host registry: codex joins lightning-run, the optimizer stays on claude-code through a separate capability, Codex gets runner table entries, additive schema and export-terms acceptance, a declared-limit path for an unverified route, parser verification and a fake host. REQUIRED_HOSTS does not change. Documentation only: nothing implemented.
